utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Can you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin, good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. General Talic, good morning to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. I can hear you in a language I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the meantime, while you are standing up, I have checked with the office -- the Registry about progress that there is or there may not be regarding the appointment of a new lead counsel. And it's being attended to and there should be a reply very soon -- confirmation, in fact, very soon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This morning very briefly, Joanna Korner, Andrew Cayley -- not briefly Andrew Cayley but briefly me -- and assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Ms. Korner. Good morning to you. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. I'm John Ackerman. I appear this morning with Marela Jevtovic and Milan Trbojevic on behalf of Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good morning to you, Mr. Ackerman. Appearances for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. I am Natasha Ivanovic-Fauveau and with Fabien Masson I represent General Talic. I should like to inform you that the registrar received yesterday all the necessary documents, and I think that the designation of Mr. Zecevic will be completed very soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. I checked with Mr. Rohde myself yesterday. I understand Mr. Ackerman wants to raise some issue this morning in private session. Is that correct, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Please let's go into private session and see what it is about and then decide whether we stay in private session or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm here to, as the expression is sometimes put, grovel, both to the Court and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not unusual in this -- in this case.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, and really to the Defence. Your Honour, it goes back to the question of Rasula's diary. Your Honour, yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- A matter arose about the adequacy of the translation. And so as a result, we decided to resubmit and in particular the disputed portion that relates to the meeting with General Talic on the 20th of April to be checked for the translation. In order to do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry about that, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's all right. In order to do that, we went back to the original scanned version to get -- to take it out for translation, and what we then discovered -- I think I'd better show Your Honour physically. We have copied the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is document 759, if I remember well. No?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And Your Honour the reason I'm here is because I introduced it into evidence. We've copied the page -- the part of the page that's been the subject of such dispute that we provided to Your Honours and to Defence counsel and the page as it appears on the system. Can I ask that that be handed to Your Honours. And there's a copy for the registrar. I think Your Honours will be able to see straight away that the top part is the original scanned version. The bottom part is what we provided. The words in Latin script do not appear on the original scanned version. We've sent someone to the evidence unit to obtain the original photocopy which has been stamped by the person who obtained the document to show that that's a copy -- an accurate copy of the original diary. And we haven't been able -- oh, I see somebody coming into court at this moment, so that may be it. And I'll ask Mr. Cayley if he can -- yes, I think it is -- just to check. We don't know how it happened. We're just effectively surmising that whoever first had a go at reading it -- who could read the language -- had difficulty in reading those particular Cyrillic words and so wrote it over the top in Latin script. And the words are in fact the same as they appear in Cyrillic, but just -- the actual original words are there but somebody has just written over the top in Latin script. And Your Honour, I have here from the evidence unit where it's been lodged since it was marked. And it's a certified copy of the original diary. And I can hand it to Your Honour, but it's the same as -- those words in Latin script do not appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The document that -- the document that you've just handed us, Ms. Korner, seems or -- that these words in Latin script are highlighted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've just highlighted them to pick them out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They're not highlighted on the copies that you had earlier or my learned friend -- counsel for the Defence. But we thought it was just easier to highlight it just to show Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think from my experience that this matter is going to end here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I would imagine that for the time being, we can leave it at that, and you prepare yourselves to bring forward whatever evidence is necessary, first to explain --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What has happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We're going to make inquiries, clearly. But as I say, this has been in the system -- or rather, in the Tribunal since 1996. We're going to see if we can find out how this happened. But I have to say realistically I think it's going to be difficult unless we can find out from records who first read the diary. The investigator or the analyst who originally acquired it has left the Tribunal but is, I know, contactable, so we'll start making inquiries to that. The other thing we're going to do, clearly, Your Honour, because of all the -- the cross-examination and the suggestions that have been made about this diary is that we are going to obtain, we hope, the actual original diary itself from Sanski Most. But Your Honour, I'm sorry. I'm afraid everybody, including us -- I mean, because we hadn't really looked at the B/C/S -- was misled by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, usually when you copy -- if you feel you shouldn't answer the question now, then don't answer it. But what puzzles me a little bit at this point in time is not exactly what happened. There may or may not be an explanation forthcoming for that. But what puzzles me for the time being is when you prepare the document for the Defence and for us and for the rest of the team, that is, when you photocopy the document that you have, which document do you use? Because it seems that from Sanski Most, you had a photocopy of the original. The original, I think, if I understood Judge Draganovic well, is still in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's absolutely right. And this is the original photocopy with a stamp on the back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That photocopy does not contain the script in Latin characters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So when you photocopied to us our copy, you must have used a copy which was not a photocopy of the original but a photocopy of a photocopy on which notes had been put or additions made. I mean, I am asking this because if you look -- and I have looked. Even I don't -- I don't understand a single word of this language, but I have gone through just out of curiosity what appears on the face of this document. And there are cancellations. There are words that are underlined. There are words that are cancelled, struck off. There are arrows. There are sort of additional notes. There are circles round certain numbers. I want to make sure that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- first of all can I explain. It happened once before, Your Honour may recall. I think when I was dealing with some of the Banja Luka documents, I noted that we had photocopied a particular document with one of the team's handwriting on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And immediately I said we'll replace it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There were others. There were others apart from that too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm afraid -- I have no objection at all of telling Your Honour what's actually happened. A photocopy of -- because the original has to be placed in the evidence unit and only brought out by signing various documents, a photocopy was kept within the Office of the Prosecutor itself, and that photocopy was used for the purposes of providing the translation. And what must have happened -- and I can only surmise -- is that when we copied for the purposes of handing it to Your Honours and the Defence -- and the Defence have had this document -- it was disclosed to them some considerable time ago in B/C/S even before the translation was obtained -- we copied in error -- we should have gone back to the original. And that's something we'll have to remember from now on -- the copy that remained in a folder within the Office of the Prosecutor itself. And unbeknownst to us, somebody had written -- as Your Honours will see, none of that underlining appears on the original. What we're going to do now is we're going to re-photocopy from the original stamped confirmed copy the whole diary, because it seems to me that's the only way we can be sure that what Your Honours and the Defence have is what we have. And we're going to resubmit -- Mr. Cayley helpfully reminds me -- all the relevant parts that are in dispute for translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ackerman and Madam Fauveau, do you have anything to say at this junction about this or not, or do you reserve your position until later when we have more information?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Some I will reserve, Your Honour. I just -- there are a number of documents that are in evidence in this case that have underlining and -- and marks and things like that. And one begins to wonder if those are part of the original document the Prosecution has or not. I also seem to recall, and I would want to check the transcript before I go much further with this -- but I seem to recall that the witness Draganovic testified that on the original which he has in Sanski Most, this Latin script appears. I think he gave -- I think he gave that testimony. But I'm not positive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't remember, Mr. -- I don't think so, but he was asked to explain how there is Latin script in a document which is otherwise entirely written in Cyrillic script, and he said "I don't have an explanation." But he -- I don't recall him saying that he was aware of the Latin script as -- having gone through the original himself. I don't recall that, anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, your recollection is usually better than mine, Your Honour, so you're probably correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, it's not a question of comparison, but -- I don't recall. I mean, I'm not excluding that he may have said so, but I don't think he did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't recall. But as Your Honour -- as I said to Your Honour, I have a number of matters I have to see to today, so I'm going to check the transcript myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I very much appreciate that, Ms. Korner. What I certainly would encourage you to do is to make sure that not where there is underlining, because this Tribunal is not going to be impressed by the fact that a certain name appears to be underlined or a certain phrase appears to be underlined. I think we are above that. However, in the document itself, there are entire lines that are cancelled.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I say -- we're going to re-photocopy from the originals --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: -- In the evidence unit and provide it. And Your Honour, there's no doubt at all and I take on board entirely what Mr. Ackerman says -- we're going to have to double-check now particularly for future documents that any underlining or things that appear on it appear on the original that we have. I mean, it's a major job. But Mr. Ackerman is absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know. And that's the last thing we needed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We need to do a double-check, and I'll start that process going immediately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Fauveau, would you like to put in your contribution on this or reserve your position?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to say that clearly the document that we received is a document that is not authentic. The suggestion of Madam Korner to give us a copy of an original copy will not assist the Defence of General Talic. I think we need to have the original, which is in Sanski Most, and that the Prosecutor should allow us to examine that real original --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we're going to attempt -- I can't promise that we can, because it's not ours to take. But we are going to attempt to get the actual original diary brought up here so that it can be examined by whoever wants to. Your Honour, all I can say is I'm sorry. I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you have difficulties, I think I can offer you a solution that I think under the Statute itself and under the Rules we are authorised if needs be to ask the particular State who has the overall responsibility of the custody of the document by way of cooperation to furnish the document with the undertaking of this Tribunal to have it returned through diplomatic channels as soon as it has served its purpose. So that can be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't anticipate there'll be any real difficulty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we do need to get an order from Your Honour, then we'll apply from it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, unless there are any other questions on this matter, can I take it that however Defence counsel would like -- I heard what Madam Fauveau said -- but would like a new photocopy of the original photocopy. Yes, she's nodding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. Yes. It's not only fair but it's important. She based part of her defence of General Talic precisely on the fact that there seem to be an -- an addition to -- so --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think it's perhaps also salutary to remember that before one shouts fraud or forgery, to wait and see. But Your Honour, there's no doubt about it, it's our fault, and we do apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No problem, Ms. Korner. This Chamber does not doubt the -- the good faith of yourself.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Your Honour, in that case, I wonder if Your Honour would be -- Your Honours would be kind enough to excuse me and Mr. Cayley will continue with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I thank you, Ms. Korner. And Mr. Cayley is ready, and Madam Fauveau, we can call the witness. And Madam Fauveau can start with her cross-examination. I forgot to ask Ms. Korner whether this was just shown to the Trial Chamber or whether it's going to be tendered in -- as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I -- I don't think the intention is to submit it as an exhibit, because what we will do is re-submit the version which doesn't have these annotations as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But she has a right to if she wants to. I think we can leave it at that for the time being. We know that there will be developments on this issue later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can I -- may I kindly ask you to repeat the solemn declaration once more, please, before you start -- recommence your evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, sir. You may sit down. As I explained to you yesterday, you're now going to be cross-examined by the Defence teams. First go is by the Defence team of General Momir Talic. Madam Fauveau, when you're ready, you may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. In the hearing of 27 May 2002, page 34 of the LiveNote, you spoke about a meeting that took place in Banja Luka in March 1991. Do you have a recollection of this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that the representatives of 17 municipalities attended that meeting. Can you tell us which municipalities were represented at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. Sanski Most, Kljuc, Prijedor, Banja Luka, Kotor Varos, Bosanska Dubica, Bosanska Gradiska, Celinac, Laktasi, Kotor Varos, Bosanska Gradiska, Bosanska Dubica, Bosanski Novi. I don't know whether they are all these 17 which belonged to the Banja Luka area, belonging -- the Banja Luka region belonging to Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you received an invitation to that meeting. Was that invitation made out in your name?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I found it on my table, on my desk.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Then how do you know that that invitation was meant for you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was my assumption. I didn't know. I was the member of the executive board. And in such a situation, if the president of the municipality couldn't attend, it would be then his second person, namely, the president of the executive council, to go. Rasula was not -- was not in Sanski Most at the time, and that is why this invitation came -- arrived to my office. And let me also add that I also asked the president of the municipality of -- Muhamed Cehajic why didn't he attend, and he said he did not receive the invitation. And the president of that municipality, Muhamed Cehajic is a Bosniak. Then I leave it to you to conclude what was happening at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to the elections of 1990, Sanski Most municipality was indeed part of the association of Banja Luka municipalities; is this true?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. Bosanska Krajina -- of Bosanska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the municipalities which you have just named, Kljuc, Prijedor, Bosanska Dubica, Bosanska Gradiska, Celinac, Laktasi -- were also municipalities that were part of the association of Banja Luka municipalities, or as you say -- as you call it, Bosanska Krajina; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way it was. Bosnia and Herzegovina was divided into these regions. That was within the framework of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss this meeting with Rasula when you returned from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not, because at that time I knew that he was attending similar such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And yet you said here in the hearing of 27 May that you enjoyed very good relations with Rasula, that you had coffee together every morning.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, also after that I would -- I was drinking coffee with him every morning, and I had very good relations with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell him that you had attended that meeting?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You made a written statement to the Prosecutor's office in 1999; is this true?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you also made a statement in Bosnia in 1995; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I gave quite a number of statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you make any other statements apart from the two that I have mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. Yes, I did. Yes. While I was living -- I was evicted to the court in Zenica. Then I made many statements to the media. I made a statement for the TV of Bosnia and Herzegovina as a witness of the programme "Witness to genocide." And I will be giving statements also in the future, because this is something which should not be forgotten.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In those statements, in the official statements that you made in Bosnia before the courts and the statement that you gave to the Prosecutor's office, you never mentioned the meeting -- this meeting which took place in March 1991. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, look, there are many -- many things that at present I haven't even touched upon. Yesterday and the day before yesterday -- this is just one small part of what I have brought forward.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned in the hearing of 27 May, page 39 of the LiveNote, about military manoeuvres which took place in Bosanski Kljuc and you said that these manoeuvres were unusual, given the war in Croatia. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter corrects. Sanski Most and Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, because I cannot remember even today whether this was before, prior to the war in Croatia or after the war began in Croatia. But I do recollect that it began in 1991, these exercises. And I knew they were unusual.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Why do you consider that this was unusual?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were unusual due to the fact that we said that these were exercises of TO of Sanski Most, Kljuc, Bosanska Krupa and Petrovac and that the mayors of all these four municipalities gave their approval for the participation of the TO units. And when I spoke with the president of the municipality of Bosanska Krupa, he told me that -- he disclosed to me that he gave no approval whatsoever concerning the organisation and the implementation of these exercises. Yes, and now I remember that also Bosanski Petrovac was included, because I remember that also the mayor of Bosanski Petrovac and the member -- president of the executive committee came both to Kljuc and to Sanski Most. And -- however, yesterday I would have stated in no uncertain terms that they did not participate. But 11 years have passed, and one cannot recollect everything immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Concerning Bosanska Krupa, could you specify what occurred there, if you are aware of it. Do you mean to say that the representative of Bosanska Krupa refused that the Bosanska Krupa people take part in this exercise and that -- and that the residents of Bosanska Krupa nevertheless did participate, or are you saying that the representatives of Bosanska Krupa did not agree and that they therefore did not participate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was not for it, and they did not participate in these exercises.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that in effect this fact that the residents of Bosanska Krupa did not take part in the exercises an unusual act and not the exercise in and of itself?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not held on the territory of Bosanska Krupa, and neither did the inhabitants of Bosanska Krupa participate in them. You see, the decision whether to participate or not is taken by the competent authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And this fact, the fact that the residents of Bosanska Krupa did not participate, is an unusual event; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, it was unusual for me because I received information that they had approved it and that they would be participating.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The military exercise in itself was a perfectly habitual event. Is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I already stated yesterday, I've seen these similar exercises in 1981, 1982, while I was still employed in the local authority bodies of Sanski Most, and I participated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thus the military exercise in itself was not unusual.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not unusual -- they would not have been unusual if it was a usual, normal time. But this wasn't the normal time for such exercises.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the situation in Yugoslavia, the war breaking out in Yugoslavia, and the disintegration of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And in what way? Is it the case that the dangerous situation should prevent military exercises?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it had then later shown itself how. Everything happened, as was foreseen in these military exercises. The red and the blue. And they -- also the attacks were carried out on the basis of the scenarios played out during the exercises.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim population had been convened -- took part in this exercise?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. And it also responded. Not only the Muslim population but also the Croat population.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So this exercise was not the exercise which had been foreseen for the Serbian population.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Yes. That was the population of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The entire population without any regard to nationality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: On 27 May, page 40 of the LiveNote, you mentioned explosions in Sanski Most. You stated that 42 buildings had been hit by explosions on one or several occasions. Do you maintain that assertion?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Prosecutor submit to the witness the written statement of July 1999 in Serbo-Croatian. Well, I believe that I will have a bit of a problem explaining where to find the paragraph I'm interested in, because the declaration -- the statement that I have does not have numbered paragraphs. I can only indicate that in English you have the Prosecutor's number 00838026 on top of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Tell me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Serbo-Croat version of the statement which is -- what is the reference number at the top of the page? And I can direct the witness to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't have the version in Serbo-Croatian. I only have the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And on the English version, it's 00838026.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that Mr. Cayley will save me from the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, it's the first paragraph, the penultimate sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I think you have to refer the witness to page 8 first of the Serbo-Croat statement, starting with the last two lines, [B/C/S spoken], and then continue over the first two lines on the next page. Have you found that paragraph, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, you may ask the question now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you look on the top of page 9 in the Serbo-Croatian version, you said: [In English] "28 shops, cafes, and restaurants were destroyed in Sanski Most area."

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was -- up till that executive board meeting when I requested that the perpetrators were to be found and determined. And I said that from then on, that the explosions increased and that in the period from the 20th to the 25th of May, even up to two explosions per day occurred, because here I state that I said twice at the meeting of the executive board. And that was up till then.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you tell us at what time this was.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the beginning of April. It means after the assembly stopped meeting, it was the 6th of -- 7th of April. And the work which was carried out by the legal authorities, the legal bodies of Sanski Most. After the assembly, it stopped meeting. The executive board never met again.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So until the beginning of April -- by the beginning of April, 28 buildings had been destroyed or damaged in Sanski Most by explosions.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You also mentioned grenades that had been launched on the mosque of Kamengrad. What is the distance between Sanski Most and the mosque?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't speaking about bombs. I spoke of two grenades which were launched. And the distance between Donji Kamengrad and Sanski Most is 7 kilometres between the two, and I'm speaking about Donji Kamengrad, because there's also Gornji or upper Kamengrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And then you went on the spot to where these explosions had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you notice any damage?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. They were -- they fell into the courtyard of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And in the courtyard, did you see traces of the explosions?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. I did. I did, and the representatives of the official organs were here. The investigator, the police force were there. And in the next few days, the -- an investigation was carried out by the lawful authorities, the lawful law and order authorities.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: On 27 May, page 45 of the LiveNote, you explained the procedure for documents, and you stated that the documents that remained in the file did not carry a stamp. In other words, those sent to the recipient did carry a stamp. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true to say that the copies sent to the recipient are in fact copies?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me put it -- according to our provisions, when a document is drafted, you first draft it, and it's clear that it has to be placed in the files. One copy is then registered in the protocol with the date, with the registration number, the signature, because the authorised person today can take out this document, then place a stamp -- stamp it, and then send it to the addressees. And I don't know whether you're informed -- to what extent you're informed. Here in the west the signature is the most important factor. While in our country, it was important to have also the stamp next to the signature, because such document -- if a stamp was placed immediately, it could be abused or misused. And that is why the file -- in the file we place a document without a stamp, with the signature but without a stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you do agree that all the copies sent to the recipient must carry the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke also of inspectors who carried money to the army in Titova Korenica, page 47 of the LiveNote. And you said that one of them lost a piece of paper that was later published by a journal in Sarajevo. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally see this lost original document? I'm not talking about what was published in the newspaper but the actual document itself.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us the name of this inspector that was involved in this case.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the crime service of the police administration in Sanski Most, Dobrijevic. I think his first name is Mirko. The surname is right. No. No. I'm sorry. Dosenovic, Dosenovic. And I think his first name is Milan. Anyway, the head of the crime department in Sanski Most at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of helicopters that went to Serb villages, and you said that those helicopters were military helicopters because there were no other helicopters flying in the area at the time; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it right to say that in fact you suppose that they were military helicopters because you assumed that there were no other helicopters in the area?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't say that I saw any insignia on the helicopters close up. That was my assumption, my assertion, and that is true, and it proved to be true.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But as far as you are concerned, it is your supposition, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't see any symbols on them, because after all, the distance was some 2 kilometres, and they were flying in the opposite direction and not over my head.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not correct to say that at the time, that is, March, April 1992, in that area members of certain international organisations and international missions deployed there did move around in helicopters?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that time. There were no missions. I would have liked to have seen that helicopter land in Kamengrad, Donji, Gornji, at least in the villages with mixed populations but not villages with 90 per cent Serb population.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But the mission of the European observers was present in the region, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know when the European observers arrived. And when you ask me about them and contacting with them before the war and after the war, I had joked with them and I said, "Your white uniforms were a symbol from Japan, because in Japan too that was a sign of something bad." And your arrival heralded the worst thing that happened to us and our people." And as for when the European observers arrived, you know that. Towards the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But they were still in the area at the beginning of 1992, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And they travelled in helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that was before their arrival, not as early as you perhaps think, April and May 1992. And especially when a helicopter flies to a village called Dabar, with 100 per cent Serb population, and within a range of some 20 kilometres -- I mean, the diameter of the village is about 20 kilometres. It's a big village. I mean area-wise. It covers a large area. Then it is quite easy to arrive there without anyone noticing it, using the hills and mountains of Grmec as concealment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You are saying that this was before the European observers arrived. Could you specify when this was?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1991. I have not remembered the exact day or month.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But in 1991, there was no prohibition on flights in Bosnia, was there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there's no point in that question. I don't know whether there was any prohibition. I was not aware of it. There were over flights in June and July of 1992 as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So in fact, there were other helicopters in addition to JNA helicopters flying in the area in 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see them, but I'm still claiming that they were army helicopters delivering weapons to the Serb people, which we established later. Because in the evening, the lights would go on in a house inhabited by a Serb, and in front of his door weapons would be left, and there were a couple of Bosniaks who just happened to have their lights on, so they too had weapons left at their doorstep.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: My question was whether at the time there were other helicopters flying there apart from JNA helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. I cannot claim 100 per cent that there were no other helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you allow for the possibility that there were others.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You spoke of your arrest at a checkpoint in March 1992 when you were returning from Sarajevo, and you said that you were arrested by a joint patrol from the police station of Mrkonjic Grad and -- consisting of police and JNA members; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar give the witness P604, 604, Exhibit 604.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, you were together with Mr. Redzo Kurbegovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the exhibit you have before you is a statement by Redzo Kurbegovic immediately after that arrest; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In that statement -- and we find it in the first paragraph -- Mr. Kurbegovic said that you were arrested by joint patrol of the Mrkonjic Grad police station, in brackets, the public security station, and by members of the JNA, in brackets, Red Berets. Is it not true that members of the JNA did not wear red berets?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that members of the JNA did not wear red berets?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them in those barracks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. One moment, Madam Fauveau, because the witness is in my opinion trying to avoid answering the question. The question is not whether you saw the soldiers wearing red berets on that occasion. The question is whether you are aware that JNA soldiers never wore red berets; in other words, that the soldiers wearing red berets on that occasion couldn't have been soldiers of the JNA but other kinds of soldiers. This is the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did understand the lady very well. That was the first time that I saw members of the army wearing red berets, members of the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I think that should satisfy you, Madam Fauveau, and you may proceed with the next question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you know that they were members of the army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: By their uniforms in the barracks. Doesn't that speak for itself?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you understand straight away that these were members of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. And I can't remember now. I had the telephone number of a colonel in Banja Luka that I wanted to call up, but they wouldn't let me do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look at page 5 of your statement in the Serbo-Croatian language and the page ending 022 of the English version, last paragraph -- ERN number 022, last paragraph. Regarding the Serbo-Croatian version, it is the last paragraph on page 5, which goes on to page 6. And you stated: [In English] "I later learned those with red berets were from Knin. They were Kninjas. They were a special police group within the regular army."

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the JNA in those days. In those days, there was the territory of Yugoslavia. Whether it was Knin or Banja Luka or Zagreb or Belgrade, it didn't matter. The only thing that matters was the military district that they belonged to. I mentioned this because it was strange for me to see for the first time these people wearing red berets.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But what I'm interested in is that in this statement, you said, "I later learned." I would like to know when did you learn that these people belonged to the JNA, later or straight away?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew it straight away. But here I said that I learnt later who those people with red berets were, that they were special units from Knin who were dispatched to the area of Bosnia-Herzegovina, specifically to Krajina, to conduct exercises, training for misdeeds.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So these people were from Knin, were they not? So you maintain what you said in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not claiming that they were from Knin. I'm claiming who else these people wearing JNA uniforms and red berets could have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And all this happened in March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago you told me that it was Yugoslavia in those days. In March 1992 Croatia was independent, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The recognition of the independence of Croatia, did it not happen on the 15th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You say that, again.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you were taken to the barracks. Where was the barracks? Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The barracks is situated about 4 to 5 kilometres from that road. And if you were to take me there now to show you where the barracks is, I would not be able to show it to you. I would not be able to find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you accept that there was no military JNA barracks within that area, that is, the area of Mrkonjic Grad?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, there was. These were huts, prefabricated huts.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: How did you know that they belonged to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, who was in them? I'm not talking about ownership. We are talking about who was in those premises and who was in possession of them at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: That is exactly what I'm asking you. How did you know that the people who were there belonged to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were dressed in uniform. They were not naked, if you -- as you're forcing me to be rude. They were wearing uniforms with insignia. And I mentioned that I found it strange that most of them - not all of them - most of them were wearing red berets.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: There were no paramilitary groups in Bosnia at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You never heard mention of the SOS group or, I don't know, the White Eagles, for instance, or Red Berets for that matter?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see. If you're talking about me and the region I come from, that was at the beginning when these started appearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you allow for the possibility that the person you saw and who arrested you on your way back from Sarajevo belonged to a paramilitary group?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because one member of the army was from Tuzla, of Croat ethnicity, Vinko, who helped us at that point in time. And things would have been much worse if it hadn't have been for him.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So this Croat had authority over the others; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, that was not what I said. I said that he helped me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: How could he have helped you if he had no authority?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, you want to beat me, and he dissuades you from doing that and manages to do so. That's what I meant. Also during the interrogation, he stops it. He says, "Stop it. That's enough. Can't you say that they're all right?" Otherwise, it could have gone on for much longer than four and a half hours if it hadn't have been for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, we approximately have another two, three minutes. If it's convenient for you to stop here. We'll stop here. Otherwise we'll continue for the next --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No microphone. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay. I understood her. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In any event, can we agree that the others were listening to what this Croat was saying even though he had no official authority?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we can't.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I'll leave it at that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Madam Fauveau. The witness can be escorted out. We are going to have a short break of 30 minutes, and we will resume at 11.00 sharp. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, while the -- excuse me, Ms. Fauveau. While the witness is coming in, just one matter that Mr. Ackerman --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The accused are not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: On what Judge Draganovic said about Rasula's diary, your recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. But let's wait -- wait for the accused to come in -- to be brought in. Yes, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Very quickly, your recollection was correct, Your Honour, of what Mr. Draganovic said. I won't read it out. It can be found at pages 5805 and 5807 of the official transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you, Mr. Cayley. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I gave you a list this morning of documents I would be using --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, yes. I was going to query whether -- which is yours and which is Madam Fauveau's, but I suppose that the one which is yours starts with P604; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No. It says "counsel for Brdjanin" on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. P69. All right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have three documents that I want to that, as a result of what has gone on so far this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 694. And you have increased your list or made some changes to your list this morning. Yes. Yes. Mr. Ackerman, just to confirm with you, we also have -- been given what purports to be documents later to be introduced by you, which is DB84; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's a document that was included as an attachment to the materials provided by the Prosecutor with regard to this witness, and I think we were not supplied a B/C/S translation of that document or any explanation that I could find of what it is. But I think on the face of it it's fairly clear what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you. Madam Fauveau, you may proceed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Prior to the pause, we mentioned your arrest at the checkpoint upon your return from Sarajevo to Banja Luka. You stated on 27 May, page 52 of the record, that you went to Sarajevo on official business on behalf of the municipality. Is this accurate? And you were with Redzo Kurbegovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whose, mine?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry about that. Please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] No. It's not your fault. Don't worry.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Redzo Kurbegovic is the chairman or the president of the SDA in Sanski Most; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that Mr. Kurbegovic went to the same meeting that you attended in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why you went to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to Sarajevo to the republican road administration, in order to complete the financing of works on the road Sanski Most-Banja Luka via Majdan and Sasine, and Redzo Kurbegovic went for other business -- party business. And since he didn't have a specific date to attend to that business, he joined me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that the last meeting of the Municipal Assembly of Sanski Most took place on the 6th and 7th of April, 1992. Is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not and, but or. Either the 6th or the 7th of April, because the session did not last for two days.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that the 6th of April is the day that the independence of Bosnia was recognised?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was so.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the hearing of 27 May, page 62 of the LiveNote, you stated that the 6th Brigade arrived in Sanski Most at the beginning of April 1992; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe it was so. But I believe it was at the beginning of that month, but I cannot tell you the precise date.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you turn to your written statement. It's in the page ending in number 022 in the English version, page 5 of the Serbo-Croatian version. It's the paragraph at the middle of the page. And you said, and I quote: [In English] "When the 6th Krajina Brigade was deployed in Sanski Most, the second half of March 1992." [Interpretation] Can you tell us when the 6th Brigade came, in March or in April?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: In April.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this written statement does not reflect the truth.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I told you I am not sure about a few days -- the dates -- the exact dates because it -- these are events of some ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: On 23 May of this year, you made corrections to this written statement. Why did you not correct that part of it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. I didn't consider this to be an essential matter. Now, at this point, I would add certain corrections to the statement. I would make some addenda.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the hearing of 27 May 2002, you stated that the checkpoints in Sanski Most were established with the arrival of the brigade at the beginning of April 1992. Is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement that you have before you, in the paragraph following, you stated: [In English] "Many checkpoints had been set up in March 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Prosecution give the 1995 statement of the witness to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If Mr. Cayley doesn't have it, I can supply it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Cayley, this was not a statement made to the to the OTP. It's a statement made -- or released to the Ministry of the Interior security service centre in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, there are two 1995 statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the statement of 13 September 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. This is the one we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you could turn to page 3 of the English version. And you mentioned there the meeting taking place on 20 April 1992. And then you state: [In English] "On that day, members of the 6th Krajina Brigade and paramilitary units of the Sanski Most SDS blocked the town, captured all its vital facilities, set up checkpoints, and limited the movement of the non-Serbian population." [Interpretation] Which of these three statements reflects the truth concerning the creation of the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question exactly. Which statements are you referring to now, the first, the second, or the third?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: On 27 May you stated that the checkpoints were created at the time of the arrival of the 6th Brigade beginning of April. In the second, which is in fact the first statement -- because it was made earlier, in 1999 -- you stated that the checkpoints were created immediately after the arrival of the 6th Brigade; in other words, in March 1992. And in the third statement, which is in fact the very first statement, because it dates back to 1995, you stated that the checkpoints were created on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting at this point because evidence is being mischaracterised by Ms. Fauveau. She knows very well these are actually referring to separate events. And the witness actually made that clear in his evidence yesterday. Whether or not the checkpoints were set up in the second half of March or early April of 1992 -- and we're talking about matters ten years ago -- frankly is not something in my view that you can put to a witness that he's lying about that, kind of fact. Moreover, what the witness said yesterday was when they arrived, checkpoints were set up. And then on the 20th of April, he said essentially that matters escalated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him tell us what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's important, Your Honour, the evidence is characterised properly and that it's not put to a witness that he's actually lying when he's talk about separate events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it has -- it's being suggested that he is lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: That's what it said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's suggested to him that he's given three different explanations or versions as to the arrival of the 6th Brigade --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Referring to different events, Your Honour. Referring to different events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But he is the witness --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour. Your Honour. Perhaps I can specify prior to the witness answering. In the 1995 statement, it's the only place where he mentioned the checkpoints, and that's why I mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sir, you have heard more or less what the question is. As a lawyer you should now have formed your mind what exactly is being required from you to answer. And you have also heard the exchange of debate between the Prosecution and the Defence. Perhaps you could now clarify the issue for us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so while -- I'm making this clear. I mean, I did not at any time understand Madam Fauveau as implying or suggesting to you that you are not telling us the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I didn't read the statement, but I could never -- never anywhere state that the checkpoints were set up on the 20th of April. I'd like to see this statement where I assert that. In concrete terms, it was the beginning of April -- the 4th of April when the 6th Krajina Brigade arrived to Sanski Most. And I also told you not to hold against me a few days earlier or a few days later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can rest assured that the Court will protect you there -- in that matter, because we can't expect -- I mean, if you ask me what happened ten years ago, I'm going to -- I'll be quite lost, even though -- though these were events which you lived and about which I would imagine you still have a very vivid memory. But anyway, Madam Fauveau, you can move to your next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could the --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. Please. I would kindly ask Madam Fauveau to show me this statement which I allegedly made on the establishment of checkpoints on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's on page 3 of the statement of 13 September 1995, the sentence beginning with: [In English] "On that day."

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it here in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I ask the usher to give me the statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it in Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So I don't have a copy in Serbo-Croat, so I can't help you much. But it is starting -- from the beginning, it should be in the third page. And just to indicate to you where you should be heading, there should be a part on the third page which indicates the date of the 25th of May. And then the names Redzo Kurbegovic, Suad Sabic, Nihad Kljucinic, Rifa Bahtic [phoen]. Right before that part where you see all these names, two sentences before, you should find the paragraph that Madam Fauveau is attributing to you as having stated to the Banja Luka police. And if you go further up, it is being suggested to you that we are definitely talking of the 20th of April of 1992. Have you found it now, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I haven't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has he been given the right statement? Because there are two statements, one very short that has got nothing to do with the question. If you have a copy -- a spare copy in Serbo-Croat, I will probably find it -- has he found it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Give it to me. Give it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'll find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, here. Here. Show it to the witness, please. This part that I have underlined, continuing to the end of the sentence. And show him also the previous page where there is the reference to the date, the 20th of April, the meeting, Talic, Rasula, and Savanovic and the rest. So he must be shown this part but also the previous page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please excuse me. I only refute Madam Fauveau stating that I had asserted that the checkpoints were set up on the 20th of April by the 6th Brigade. I would like her to find that, where I've stated that. And I do not question the date, 20th of April, and the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour -- the President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sir, you have the statement in Serbo-Croat. I have marked on that page with pencil the beginning of the sentence that I would like you to read. And then tell us what it says. That is the part of the statement which you gave in Banja Luka way back on the 13th of September, 1995, at least according to the document that we have, and that's where Madam Fauveau is alleging that you stated that checkpoints were set up on the 20th of April of 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am just asking that Madam Fauveau shows it to me and that she reads it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sir, I have indicated on that page the sentence that you are required -- requested to read. I'm not going to ask Madam Fauveau, because Madam Fauveau has already indicated the paragraph to the Chamber. And that's on the basis of what she indicated that I am indicating the sentence to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've seen this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And what does it say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That they blocked and encircled the town. And there's a difference between blocking the town and it's something else to set up checkpoints in the town. Well, you know, the establishment of checkpoints means that you're cutting off the traffic routes. It means that you're stopping the traffic, that you're searching the vehicles. And this was encircling and -- the encircling and the blocking of the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This happened when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That happened on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And before --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rather, it happened earlier. It happened already on the 17th of April, when we were in the municipal building. And on the 19th of April --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what's written in the Serbo-Croat version. Can I see the version that the witness has before his eyes. Can the usher give me the version that the witness has before him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the mark which -- the part which I have marked in pencil, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "On that day, the members of the 6th Krajina Brigade together with SDS Sanski Most paramilitary formations blocked the town. They occupied all the vital facilities in the town, set up checkpoints, and limited the movement of non-Serb population."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you did indeed state that on that day, the members of the 6th Brigade established checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, together with what I stated beforehand, namely, blocking. And in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There were several occasions when checkpoints were set up. And I think we can leave it at that and move to the next topic or subject or question or whatever, because this is getting us nowhere. You know, I mean, it's -- it more or less confirms what Mr. Cayley has suggested. But Mr. Cayley, you have to understand that as much as possible, I mean, we try to avoid -- because now the explanation has come forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Of course --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You were suggesting -- you were opposing objecting on the basis that he was being called a liar. He was not being call add liar.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: When somebody is asking if they're telling the truth or not, I think that's a suggestion they may be lying. The only thing I'd add, Your Honour, is this, these statements are not transcripts -- verbatim transcripts of conversations. I know that, the Defence knows that. They are a summary of what a witness can say. That's all it is. And to put these sort of captured lines to a witness in this fashion is in my view not an entirely fair process.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: He hasn't been lying about these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No one is saying --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: It's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- He's been lying, and in fact I'm sure he hasn't. But it's a question of he was explaining there were different days on which checkpoints were set up, and on this particular occasion you have what according to him is a complete blockade of the town.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to explain it a bit further. The establishment of checkpoints is the establishment of checkpoints, while the blockade implies a blockade plus checkpoints in some other places, additional checkpoints. And that was the worst --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have explained it already. At least the Chamber has understood what you mean, in any case, and that's why I'm suggesting to Madam Fauveau to move ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher show the witness Exhibit P608.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this an order of the command of the 5th Corps, dated the 1st of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me a lot, but I assume it is, yes, because this document bears everything that is necessary, confidentiality, who it has been drafted by, to whom it is addressed. It is signed by the competent person.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that in paragraph 2, in the second paragraph on page 1, which is below the paragraph marked number "1," General Talic ordered that the establishment of barricades should be prevented?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not prevented. It was intensified, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you what the order says, preventing setting up roadblocks.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So he did request the prevention of the setting up of roadblocks, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We demanded that on the 20th of April as well, when we all had a meeting together.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether in this order dated the 1st of April he already ordered that setting up roadblocks be prevented.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can say that; I cannot. Because we made the same demand on the 20th of April, identical to what he ordered here.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you read out that paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean paragraph 2 of point 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Precisely, yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, no. I tell him whether he should read it aloud or not. Everyone has it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it's not a good translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Point it out.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He doesn't wish to answer my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. Point out where the discrepancy in the translation is and we'll put a direct question to him, after all you are --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English version it appears as if this establishment of roadblocks was ordered, whereas in fact it was the opposite. It's not clear, in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It is clear to the Trial Chamber, Madam Fauveau it says what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think there's a comma that may make it unclear. But I don't think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. "Achieving" only refers to the first part. "Achieving control of the territory." And then "preventing inter-ethnic conflict, setting up roadblocks and securing features of special importance." So ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's not quite clear whether the word "preventing" relates also to the second part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Put the question. Put the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please confirm that General Talic ordered that the setting up of roadblocks should be prevented.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But to whom?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it an order addressed to the command of the 6th Partisan Division, is it not -- to the 10th Partisan Division. I correct myself. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said what I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it an order addressed to the 10th Partisan Division?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Answer that question, please, sir. Otherwise you're going to end up being --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have a document in front of you. You are a lawyer. You are being asked a simple question. You are being asked whether this order is addressed according to the document, on the face of the document to the 10th Partisan Division. Answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of a meeting that held -- was held on the 20th of April, 1992. Is it correct to say that the meeting was organised upon the initiative of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And the invitation was sent by the Serb side.
