utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So the meeting was not organised in response to your demands.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar give the witness Exhibit P759.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you did not recognise Rasula's handwriting; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you personally cannot say whether this diary is indeed Rasula's diary or not.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I do not have a talent for recognising people's signatures. I've never done it in my life.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You personally cannot confirm that this diary does indeed belong to Rasula.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't deny it either.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you find page with the number of the 5th of November and refers to the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is the -- page 15 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm unable to find it here, that particular page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the page which has --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's the page which at the top has got the following number, 00379442. Next to it there is the entry 5th November. All right? Did he find it now? I thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the very bottom of this page, you find the name that was pronounced by General Talic, Kupres, Bosanski Brod, and Vukovar. You said yesterday that certain Muslims took this to be a threat; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that in Kupres in April 1992 the Serb population was massacred by the Croats?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it not true that on the 26th of March, 1992 at Sijekovac, Bosanski Brod municipality, the Serb population was massacred and expelled by the Croats?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that at the end of this meeting, you requested that the conclusions be announced over the radio and that the director of the radio, Orlovic, said that that was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that it was technically unfeasible.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: On page 3 of your statement from 1995, you said that Orlovic actually said that it was impossible and that he didn't want to do it because this did not suit the leaders of the SDS. This second part of your statement, that is, that it did not suit the leaders of the SDS, was that -- is that part correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember ever saying that. I said that we asked that he make this public and that he said it was technically impossible to do that, and we said that it was possible for a telephone to be used in the office and for the statement to be made directly -- broadcast live on the radio. But the general said that he was in a hurry to get back. And you resolve your problems and questions this evening at 6.00 p.m. when you can have a meeting here to deal with those problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1995 you said: [In English] "Mihajlo Orlovic was one of those responsible at the Sanski Most radio said that it was impossible to do that then, and he did not want to announce that later either because it did not suit SDS leaders and representatives of the military structures." [Interpretation] I know that until the 25th of May that was never broadcast. Whether it was later, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that you saw General Talic on television cordially greeting leaders of the SDS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he was in the first row. The camera shot a close-up of these people.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The occasion at which General Talic was with the SDS leaders was this celebration of the liberation of Banja Luka at the end of the Second World War, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was. I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And that celebration was held every year, was it not? Even before 1990 these celebrations were a regular event; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. Yes. We had similar celebrations in Sanski Most. The 20th of October, which was celebrated every year. So I assume that was what happened in Banja Luka. I can't claim that because I didn't go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: As regards Banja Luka, like other towns, would you agree that it was quite normal for representatives of the army should be present during a ceremony of that kind?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday that after this meeting of the 20th of April, the situation in Sanski Most did not improve. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P622.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this is a regular report of the command of the 5th Corps dated the 23rd of April, 1992? Regular combat report.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the paragraphs after number 3, it says: [In English] "According to reports received, there have been no significant changes in the situation on the ground. Destruction of individual buildings, threats, and blackmail and conflicts between individuals are still occurring." [Interpretation] Does this description correspond to the actual situation in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It would if it said that on the -- it should have said that on the ground, the situation has deteriorated, rather than "no significant changes have occurred." And the mention of conflicts between individuals, it is not indicated between which individuals.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look at your written statement from 1999 that you gave to the OTP. In the English version, it is the page with the number ending with the number 025.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what page is it in my version?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll tell you in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's page 8, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Page 8.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the paragraph relating to the Territorial Defence, the paragraph beginning with the words [In English] "The Serbs did not establish any official Serbian TO."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] It's in the middle of the page, sir, the paragraph "Srbi nisu osnovaci," whatever.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In the middle of that paragraph, you said: [In English] "The Sanski Most TO weapons were kept in the military barracks in Prijedor pursuant to the 1990 order." [Interpretation] Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. Up to a point.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And if you have the English version of it, please put it on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this indeed the 1990 order that you referred to in your written statement? Let me rephrase my question. Paragraph 1 of this document, does it refer to the same order that you are referring to in your written statement?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, but it's difficult for me to say looking through such a lengthy document. But tell me specifically what you want from me regarding this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 1 of this document, does it refer -- [In English] "Pursuant to the order of the head of the Chief of Staff."

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, oh, I see. SFRY, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The order mentioned in this paragraph, is that the same order that you referred to in your written statement?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when the weapons of the Sanski Most Territorial Defence were transferred to Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of a meeting that took place on the 24th of May with a certain Nedjeljko Anicic. And you said yesterday on page 23 of the LiveNote, "At the time Nedjeljko Anicic was not a member of the Territorial Defence." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What year? The 24th of May, but what year?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember any meeting being held on the 24th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not interested so much in the meeting but in the fact that you said that Mr. Nedjeljko Anicic was not a member of the Territorial Defence in those days.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What happened after the 17th of April, I don't know. I don't know what the SDS did in the area, because nothing was legal. All I can assert is that up until the 17th of April, Anicic did not head the Territorial Defence and the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you do allow for the possibility that in May, Anicic was a member of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me say I can only speak for the period up to the 17th of April and not later, because later I don't know. It was all illegal and violent.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the registrar show the witness Prosecution Exhibit P338. [In English] 638.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness has already seen this document, because actually the same question that you have put was put to him by Mr. Cayley or whoever, whether he knew Mr. Anicic was head of the territory -- anyway, please proceed with your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is the document of the Territorial Defence; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the very top of the first page, it is apparently signed by the commander, Colonel Anicic; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way it should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you turn to the last page of the document. The date of 26 May is mentioned twice; right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the last page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the last page.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here I can see the 26th of May mentioned once, at 50500. And then I see the second time, the mention made of 26 of May, 0400.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the very bottom of the page, you see recipients for this document. Is that exact?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Amongst the recipients, do you find the 6th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not see it. If it's not the 1st Serbian Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But the Territorial Defence was clearly made up of these battalions; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know, particularly if you consider a Territorial Defence unit of a local commune, that would be a smaller unit. It wouldn't be a battalion of men.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But since we see here that it is a Serbian Territorial Defence, which you were not very much aware of or familiar with, rather, can you accept the possibility that this battalion is a battalion of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "1st Serbian Battalion." I cannot tell you to whom it belonged.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were arrested on 25 May 1992; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Yes, on the 25th.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: It was on the 25th of May, 1992; yes?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that at the time of your arrest, there was fighting going on in Mahala?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was never any fighting going on in Mahala. And in -- on May 25th, it wasn't the case either.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that prior to the 25th of May, prior to your arrest, you saw an attack of any kind in Mahala?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: After the 25th of May, did you personally witness any kind of attack on Mahala?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You were detained -- after your arrest on 25 May, you were detained at the police station of Sanski Most; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In the prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did this prison belong to the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was within the walls of the compound of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that you did not have the possibility of listening to the radio during your detention in Sanski Most prison. Is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Sometimes when we'd go out to lunch, we would hear the guards were listening to the radio, and so we would hear something.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: But when you were locked up in your cells, you could not hear the radio; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned murders taking place in Hrustovo and Vrhpolje. Do you remember stating that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: When these murders were committed, you were in prison; is this true?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you personally did not see these murders taking place.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Hence you don't know exactly what happened in Hrustovo and Vrhpolje during your detention; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard from others what the others experienced, but I personally never saw it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The persons who told you about what happened, did they tell you that the Muslims arrested 46 Serbian officers in that place?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you that the persons who arrested these Serbian officers were armed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you are aware of the fact that there was fighting going on in Vrhpolje and Hrustovo.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You stated yesterday that up to 10 June, page 47 of the LiveNote, that you were not mistreated in the prison. Is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up till the 9th. Up till the 9th of June.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the case that the other persons who were detained with you in the prison were mistreated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Up to the 9th of June for the time being, because --

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those who were in my cell together with me, they were not mistreated.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what treatment was given to persons in other cells, if you are aware of it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know. I believe that they weren't beaten either, due to the fact that we would be let out from the cells simultaneously. And on the other hand, I never heard shouts or other suffering; therefore, I assume they were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was Adil Draganovic detained during that period in the same prison as you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is, from the day you were admitted to that prison until the 9th of June. These are the dates that you have to refer to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. However, Adil Draganovic was in cell number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned a transfer of the prisoners from that prison to Manjaca on 6 June 1992. Do you recall stating that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher show the witness Exhibit 666.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this an order dated 6 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And pursuant to that order, the police station is given charge of the transfer of 150 prisoners to Manjaca; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the very bottom of the order --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because I'm beginning not to understand now. The way the interpretation goes is as follows. The witness was asked: "And pursuant to that order, the police station is given charge of the transfer of 150 prisoners to Manjaca." Okay. Yes, you may go ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: At the very bottom of the page, there are two recipients of the order; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it. Is this under item 10?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who this order was addressed to.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: He doesn't -- he doesn't have the right document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... he definitely doesn't have the right document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you now have before you an order dated 6 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to this order, the public security station is ordered to transfer 150 prisoners to Manjaca; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it should be.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And at the bottom left of the document, you can see that the document was addressed to two recipients -- in fact, one, because the other one was filing. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: According to this document as it stands, it was not addressed to a military organ; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: During your detention, you were transferred to Betonirka. Can you tell us who was in charge of Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated yesterday who the -- was running, who was the head of the camp, and who was the deputy chief. Drago Vujanic, he was the director and Krunic Mico was his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: These persons were members of the police; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drago Vujanic was, while Krunic covered different positions in different areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You stated yesterday, page 59 of the LiveNote, that you were never beaten by someone called Tonci in Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. There were also others who didn't beat me; not only Tonci.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you turn to your statement, your written statement of 1999. In the English version, it's the page ending with 028, third paragraph in the English version. And it's at page 11, third paragraph of the original Serbo-Croat.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Let me find it on page 11. I do not have page 11 here in this text.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's page 11 of the written statement of 1999.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1999. This one is 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The second sentence, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, let him read -- let him read for himself first the entire paragraph. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Can I also point out, Your Honour, this is a matter that was corrected in the corrected statement. Because actually if you read the English version, it doesn't make any sense at all in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will return to the correction.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In effect you corrected this statement on the 23rd of May. Unfortunately I only have the English version of that correction. And you stated: [In English] "On that occasion, Tonci beat me and Tonci told me that he was beating me on the orders of Mirko Vrucinic." [Interpretation] And what I'm interested in -- in fact, this doesn't change much, because what I'm interested in was not corrected, remains the same. You said that Tonci beat you once; whereas yesterday you said that Tonci did not beat you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I gave that statement in the context that Mirko Vrucinic, in connection with my -- he was kind to my sisters and my wife, allowing them to visit me occasionally, to bring me medicines, cigarettes, and clothing. And Tonci called me -- called me once out at 4.30 and was beating me till 6.30. Once again, when he was at a shift, he beat me again. And the third time he beat me -- and the third time after half an hour of beating me, he said, "Mirzo, please sit down," and he told me, "You know, I never beat anyone except you, and I'm beating you at the orders of Mirko Vrucinic. I won't be beating you any more, but I will be provoking you." And I made this statement in this context to show that on the one hand he was helping to -- helping my family, my wife, my sister, showing as if he was wishing me the best, and on the other hand he was ordering this guard to beat me and to mistreat me. This is the statement that I wanted to make.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Why is it the case that yesterday, page 59, in the question of the OTP was: [In English] “Did at any time a person named Tonci beat you at the Betonirka?” [Interpretation] And you replied, "No."

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said no at that moment because even the beatings I did receive, I didn't consider him -- his beatings but beatings he carried out as orders of others. I understood it as a question whether also he beat other detainees. And this -- I would never make this statement. There are many other statements I could give. But this was specific. On the one hand, he was helping; on the other hand, he is forcing others to beat me. And that was the Serbian policy at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this Tonci beat you on the orders of someone, of Vrucinic; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the orders of Mirko Vrucinic. And if he told me an untruth, then I'm not speaking the truth here either.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the others, the others who beat you, beat you of their own volition.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe so, because people came from the street to beat us. And may I add, there were also fine people who tried to oppose this, and not all guards beat us and not every -- they weren't all the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: On 7 July 1992, is it the case that you returned to the prison located within the compound of the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I came back to the same prison, the same cell from which I previously left for the Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And the representative of the International Red Cross came to visit you in that prison; is this the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. And they also took our names and registered us.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you had had opportunity to speak to them about the presence of -- outside of the presence of the guards.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We -- we talked alone with the representative of the Red Cross and an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: In order to clarify, you were alone with the International Red Cross representative and with an interpreter, but there were no guards present; is this accurate?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, alone. And the other detainees weren't present either. And this is the way the discussion was carried out with all the detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps we could go to a break now, because I'm going to change subjects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what I was going to suggest to you, that it's a suitable time to go have our break.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any event, I'll be able to conclude today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we'll have a break of 30 minutes, resuming at 1.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, I went to see my client for a moment, and I wasn't told that we were convening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] That's okay. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You were transferred to Manjaca on the 28th of August, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: During the transport to Manjaca, you were not mistreated; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: How many people were transferred with you on that day to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: 48, and with me 49.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Was anyone among that group of people mistreated during the transport?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me give you an answer. When the bus reached the police station compound, there were 15 of us originally. Two stayed behind. Thirteen of us reached the bus. And one of the guards -- actually, one of the escorts, whose name I cannot recall, had an automatic weapon, and he said, "Sit down wherever you like. And until we reach Manjaca, no one may give you a dirty glance, never mind touch you in any way." And that is how it was. The 13 of us who were in prison reached the Krings Hall where another 36 people were loaded onto the bus. And then we were driven to Manjaca. Let me also point out that we took the shortest possible route to get there, without any kind of mistreatment whatsoever or any harassment of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The day you arrived at Manjaca, that is, the 28th of August, 1992, you said that a group of prisoners were released on that day is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know how many people were released on that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please don't take it against me if I'm not accurate, but I think it was 60 or 61 persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said yesterday, page 70 of the LiveNote, that the prisoners had no covers in Manjaca. Is it not true that the International Red Cross brought covers?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that that was what the detainees told me, who had arrived there before me.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So when you were in Manjaca, you did have a cover or blanket.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So actually, you were talking about the conditions in the Manjaca camp in June 1992, but you personally were not there in those days, were you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not. I said what I had heard from other detainees.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you personally had no direct knowledge of the conditions in Manjaca in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no direct knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: When did you leave the Manjaca camp?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 31st of October, 1992. I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you were exchanged, were you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And how many people from Manjaca were exchanged on that same date with you, that is, the 31st of October, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were 56 of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: During the hearing on the 27th of May, you mentioned the referendum that took place on the 28th of February and the 1st of March, 1992. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar show the witness Exhibit P104.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have before you a two-page document?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that this document was distributed to the Serbs before the referendum in Bosnia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was distributed.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 2 of that document, the page entitled "[Previous translation continues] What the life in Bosnia mean?" [Interpretation] Would you look at the words "written" right underneath that title.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] "There is no peace or co-existence between the Islamic faith and non-Islamic social and political institutions." [Interpretation] Do you agree that this is an abstract taken from the Islamic declaration?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar show the witness Defence Exhibit DT14, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately I don't have an English version of this document. And in French, it is page 42. The first column and the last line of the first column and then it goes on into the second column. Sir, will you look at page 22 of that document. In paragraph 3, the second sentence, isn't it the same sentence that you find on document P104 of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't compared the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you look, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's illegible. This copy is illegible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What page is it in the Serbo-Croat version, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Serbo-Croat version, it is page 22, third paragraph. And the second sentence of that paragraph. In document P104, it is the first sentence below the title on the second page of that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is it the same sentence?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I read to the witness the sentence from the book in Serbo-Croatian?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does he have a copy of that page? Do you have page 22 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you look at the third paragraph, starting with [B/C/S spoken]. That's the first sentence. The next sentence reads [B/C/S spoken]. This is the sentence that Madam Fauveau --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that. I have that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So what you are being asked now is to look at the previous document, the declaration, in other words, in Serbo-Croat, obviously. And if you can read that. The first sentence after the title, after the name of Alija Izetbegovic, whether what's written there is exactly the same as what you've read on page 22 of Izetbegovic's Islamska Deklaracija [phoen].

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see here the name "Izetbegovic." I'd like to see it regardless.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, on which document are you looking for the name Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here. I know that this is from his declaration.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe the witness doesn't have the same document that I have. I just don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Bring the document, please, over to me so that I can confirm whether he has the right document or not. It's the single page that I want to see. Yes, he has the right document. Ask him -- Usher, come here, please. Ask him to look at this and the next three lines and the reference to page 22 and to tell us what he can read from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Be patient.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I -- yes, yes, I've found it. I was looking for it in this other text. You didn't tell me that it was the subtitle. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that's exactly a reproduction of -- a faithful reproduction of the text from Mr. Izetbegovic's book; no?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Nothing, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that this document, P104, page 2, consists in fact of extracts from the Islamic declaration?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, we are not discussing faith here. I still claim that religions differ. I claim that. We are discussing religions here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The question was a very simple one: Do you agree that on the face of it, page 2 of this document does nothing else but make specific reference, in quotes, to parts -- different parts from Mr. Izetbegovic's Islamic declaration? It has got nothing -- we are not discussing religion here. It's the last thing that this Trial Chamber wants to embark upon. It has enough trouble.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we are embarking upon it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, look at page 2 of the document and tell me whether it -- it reproduces in quotes from different --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's all we wanted to know. Yes, Madam Fauveau, next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Islamic declaration was written by Alija Izetbegovic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And Alija Izetbegovic was president of the SDA of Bosnia, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: And he became president of the independent state of Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. President of the presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly. Could you please look at the last sentence of the third paragraph. We are still talking about page 22 of the Serbo-Croatian version. Page 42, second column, last sentence before the paragraphs written in italics in the English version -- in the French. I'm sorry. Is it true that Alija Izetbegovic wrote "there is therefore no principle of secular government, and the state should be an expression and support for the moral concepts of religion"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I received in the interpretation, that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 3 of the Islamic declaration, page 11 -- page 1, sorry, of the French version. The last part -- the last paragraph of the first part: "The realisation of Islam in all walks of private life of individuals in the family and in society through the renaissance of Islamic religious thought and the creation of a single Islamic community from Morocco to Indonesia." Is that what was written there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Wasn't that the programme of the SDA, to create an independent Muslim state?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau. Now, Mr. Karabeg, you are now going to be cross-examined for the next 25 minutes or so by Mr. Ackerman, who is the lead counsel for Radoslav Brdjanin. And then we will continue obviously tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before Mr. Ackerman begins, I should like to ask for the admission into evidence of Exhibit DT14, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Fauveau. It is so admitted. Thank you. You don't have any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Alija Izetbegovic's -- yeah. No, I have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry. I took it for granted. Sorry I didn't ask you, Mr. Cayley. Thank you. You can start when you're ready, Mr. Ackerman. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thanks, Your Honour. I'm just trying to get organised here. I'll be ready in a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Karabeg.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: As the Judge told you, my name is John Ackerman. I will ask you some questions about the things that you are familiar with regarding these issues. The first thing I want to ask you is this: On the 23rd of May, just a few days ago, you had an opportunity with an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor to go through your statement of 24/25 July 1999 and make corrections to that statement, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And that actually resulted in a new statement that you signed, which basically set out those corrections, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Since that -- since those events, that time you spent with the representative of the OTP going through your statement and making those changes, have other things occurred to you in your original 1999 statement that you now realise are incorrect and that you would like to change?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me say I wouldn't change anything. But corrections were made mainly due to an erroneous translation of an important part of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I fully understand that. My question really is not about why you made corrections. My question is: At this moment, are you aware of any other parts of that statement that you would like to correct before I begin to ask you questions about it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. We'll forge ahead and you can just tell me. Do you have there before you your statement of 24/25 July 1999? I think it's right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told that the witness's answer to my question about whether there was anything he wanted to change properly translated was "I will keep that answer to myself." And it has been translated "I cannot answer that now." I'd like to clarify that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Karabeg, have you followed what Mr. Ackerman has just tried to explain to me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: When he asked you this question: At this moment, are you aware of any other parts of that statement that you would like to correct before I begin to ask you questions about it," what was your answer? Was your answer "I will keep that answer to myself," or "I cannot answer that question now"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I will keep that answer to myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, I would ask you to ask him to answer that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And you need to answer that question, because it's an important question. You are obviously going to be asked about your statement, and it's also in your interests to answer that question. The question is -- I will repeat it. At this moment, apart from the corrections you have made, are you aware of any other parts of your statement that you would like to correct before Mr. Ackerman begins to ask you questions about your statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just say one thing, Your Honour. I mean, this is traditional sort of cross-examination trick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman wants a blanket statement. No, this statement is absolutely perfect. And then he's going to -- why doesn't he just direct him to the parts of the statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. But the witness is also a lawyer, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: But we could get right to it and we could move much more quickly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not a trick. And I resent it being called a trick. That is not fair --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, let's take it -- let's take it that the Trial Chamber knows exactly what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I might agree that it's a technique. Trick is not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Technique. We all put that question when there is a statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's an appropriate way to do it, so I resent it being called a trick. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karabeg, answer that question. It's in your interest to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if I were to change it, I would really expand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I experienced quite a lot of these things -- many of these things, and I've seen many of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Ackerman, you can safely proceed to the next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So it is your position that you stand by what's contained in that statement with the exception of the changes that you made on the 23rd of May.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If you will look, sir, at what probably is the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And I'm going to get some assistance here, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It probably is the second page. It has the number in the English version -- if number 20 at the top. In the B/C/S version, it has number 52 at the top. And it's a paragraph that begins with this language: "The members of the executive board." And it's the third full paragraph on that page that has the number ending in 52. So if you look at the very top, you'll see a number ending in 52. And then the third full paragraph says: "The members of the executive board of the SDS." Do you see that? Very near the top, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I haven't -- yes. Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right. The last sentence of that paragraph: "I do not have first-hand information on the functions of the Crisis Staff, and all I know is only hearsay and rumours." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, what Crisis Staff it is that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was thinking that it was the defence staff of the municipality, which I was heading as the head -- the leading person of the executive body. And it consisted of the president of the municipality, the head of the police, the head of the defence, and the head of Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: So this was the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most municipality essentially that you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: On the first day that you testified -- it's LiveNote page 59, Mr. Cayley -- you told us that when Mr. Vrkes was talking about -- about a time that Mr. Vrkes was talking about pressure coming from Banja Luka to integrate Banja Luka into the region. You recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And you told us that he mentioned the names of Brdjanin and Krajisnik as putting pressure on him in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that that issue should be placed on the agenda. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: But what I'm focussing on is you say that he mentioned the names of Brdjanin and Krajisnik as putting pressure on him in that regard. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the relationship that existed at that time between Mr. Brdjanin and Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Don't you know that Mr. Krajisnik was not even from Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Don't you know that Mr. Brdjanin was from Celinac?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Would you concede that you might be mistaken about what he told you and that he didn't say the names Brdjanin and Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want you to look now at your statement again. And it is the next paragraph after the one we had looked at earlier. It begins with the language "from late March and April 1992." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: How does it begin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It begins with "From late March and April 1992."

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay. You said that the main issue, the main SDS issue, was that the municipality of Sanski Most must become part of Republika Srpska and attached to the regional -- to the regional in Banja Luka -- the region in Banja Luka; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And then you said: "In early April 1992, Vrkes said in the assembly sessions that there was a lot of pressure about this matter from the leadership of Banja Luka. He did not mention any names." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the official assembly meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And when you gave this statement to the Prosecutor in 1992, you knew that it was in connection with the charges against Mr. Brdjanin and Mr. Talic, didn't you? I'm sorry. In 1999. When you gave the statement in 1999, you knew it was in connection with these charges?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: When you came here and talked with the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor regarding any additions or corrections to your statement, you knew it was in connection with the case against Brdjanin and Talic, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only when I came here. Only then I knew that it referred to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And in the process of making changes to your statement, you didn't make any change to include this statement that you mentioned in your testimony, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you in what sense I would make corrections.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And in fact, nowhere in your statement to the OTP or your other two statements that were made to Mr. Ibric -- Zijad Ibric did you ever mention the name Mr. Brdjanin, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- it is my first time that I'm seeing Mr. Brdjanin here -- after arriving here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. Now, when you say that it was the -- the main issue raised by the SDS that Sanski Most must become part of the RS attached to the centre of the region in Banja Luka -- when you talk about the region in Banja Luka, what are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something which was to be done under duress, violent, and something in a negative context, because at that last meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Something happened in between my question and answer that -- it's probably my fault that you didn't understand my question. You talked about the SDS position that it wanted Sanski Most to become part of the -- and I think your words -- "attached to the centre of t the region in Banja Luka." What exactly are you referring to when you talk about the region in Banja Luka? What specifically does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the term "region of Banja Luka," I'm referring to that what was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, all --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Namely, it was the detachment from the Republika Srpska and the merging, integration with Yugoslavia. I would like to correct myself. The division and separation from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the unification with Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, already for quite some time Sanski Most had been part of a community of Bosnian Krajina municipalities centred in Banja Luka, hadn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not in the way that it was required of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it was not translated properly, and I'll try it again, Your Honour. Sanski Most for some time had been part of what was known as the community of Bosnian Krajina municipalities, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: That was about 20 municipalities that combined to form that community of Bosnian Krajina municipalities, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not 20, but to be precise 17 municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P69 B, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And please conclude in the next minute, Mr. Ackerman; otherwise, resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'll have to resume tomorrow. We can't do that. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So leave Exhibit P69 over there. Mr. Karabeg, we are going to stop here for today. You will be escorted out of this courtroom, back to your -- where you're staying, and we will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. I owe you an apology for starting a little bit late this morning. The reason was again, once more, we had some procedural issues relating to the trial that we needed to debate and decide upon. It had nothing to do with your testimony or with you. But please accept our apologies for keeping you waiting in the room for a few minutes. I thank you, sir, and you may withdraw now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything you wish to tell me before -- okay. I thank you. We'll meet again tomorrow morning at 9.00 sharp. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 1.46 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 30th day of May, 2002, at 9.00 a.m.
